svg.title: Claude asks whether the task list builds the design in an acceptable order, with the options Approved and Changes needed; the author picks Approved, and Claude says the spec is in .freethinking/specs/design-skills/ and the next step is /freethinking:implement-spec design-skills.

g.text: freethinking — start-task
⏺ AskUserQuestion(questions: [{"question": "Do these tasks build the design in an order you
accept?", "header": "Approve", "options": [{"label": "Approved", "description": "The task list
stands as written; implement-spec builds it from wave 0."}, {"label": "Changes needed",
"description": "Say what is missing or wrong in the free text and I will revise."}],
"multiSelect": false}])
Your questions have been answered: "Do these tasks build the design in an order you
accept?"="Approved". You can now continue with these answers in mind.
● The spec is approved and its three files are in `.freethinking/specs/design-skills/`:
`requirements.md`, `design.md` and `tasks.md`.
Next step: run `/freethinking:implement-spec design-skills`. It starts at wave 0, the six tasks
that put the templates, the reviewer agent, the three skills and the issue-form entries on disk
together, so `make validate` passes at the end of the wave. Wave 1 is the description clause, the
README and version, the ten eval cases and the Makefile lines. Wave 2 is yours: the eval runs.
Two things before you start it:
- **Branch.** This worktree is detached at origin/main, not on `main` by name, so
implement-spec's set-up will not offer to create the branch. Create `design-skills` first with
`git checkout -b design-skills`, or tell me and I will do it outside the skill.
- **Ticket.** The `pr` skill wants an issue. If you file one before the PR, the branch becomes
`<number>-design-skills` and the pull request closes it on merge; I can draft the issue body from
the requirements whenever you want.
2026-10-20 · freethinking 0.14.0
